Answer: C
Reason: The lateral view (Figure 1b) clearly demonstrates a large mass located in the posterior aspect of the thorax, displacing the aerated lung tissue anteriorly. The frontal view (Figure 1a) shows opacification of the right hemithorax with preservation of the tracheal midline position and lack of significant cardiac shift to the left, consistent with a posterior mediastinal mass compressing the right lung without causing major mediastinal displacement.
